> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `09dffc6d0108cd9935d5445efe8215e4ee5da84c` — the merge of head `03a9717ca74695f7f9b8ea238fdae69611d7dfc3` into base `459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 09dffc6d0108cd9935d5445efe8215e4ee5da84c && git checkout 09dffc6d0108cd9935d5445efe8215e4ee5da84c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca 03a9717ca74695f7f9b8ea238fdae69611d7dfc3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca && git merge --no-ff 03a9717ca74695f7f9b8ea238fdae69611d7dfc3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 459afea1f69ff69422de2a7a2c7674b6f7ea1aca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `03a9717ca74695f7f9b8ea238fdae69611d7dfc3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (`vetOrganizationClaim`), packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts (`postureEnforcesWall`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts (`resolveDelegatorContext`, `buildContextForUser`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`composeReadableIdsAtBoundary`, the engine's `getReadFilter` call site), packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-record-read-gate.ts (the header flag), docs/adr/0021-analytics-dataset-semantic-layer.md (D-C), .changeset/25106-read-scope-delegated-organization-membership.md (② only: its level and its declaration lines)

Rendered at 2026-10-22T01:18Z on card #25106's body and all eight comments, PR #25150's body, file list and net diff against `main` at this head (the PR base `459afea1f` is the merge base and the current `origin/main`, so the two-dot and three-dot diffs are one: 3 files, +192/−2), and the head's check-runs. Ruling of record: seat call `6328262579` (option A, the provider mirror) under claim `6328928374`. Disclosure (#9387, `5323310017`): this record states the rule, the narrowing and the verdict abstractly.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The one accept-set change, confined to `computeDelegatedReadFilter`: right.** The net diff to `security-plugin.ts` is two hunks, both inside that private method (its docblock, and one branch in its body); nothing else in the file moves — not `getReadFilter`, not `resolveOperationPrincipals`, not `canReadObject`. The method has one caller, `getReadFilter`'s delegated branch, so the narrowing reaches exactly what that branch serves: the published `security` service's `getReadFilter` answer (the analytics read-scope bridge, and the engine's `ReadableIds` composition) for a context that carries the delegation link. No export is added or changed, no rule text is duplicated and no error code is added: the branch answers the existing `RLS_DENY_FILTER` sentinel by reference, as every other deny in the method does, and logs at `warn`, as the prologue's refusal does.

**(b) The refused cells are exactly the prologue's, under both walled postures: right.** Read side by side, the new branch and the prologue's branch (`resolveOperationPrincipals`, the `resolved` arm after the dangling-delegator refusal) compute the live organization by the same expression (a non-empty `tenantId`, stringified), hand `vetOrganizationClaim` the same three inputs — that organization, the delegator context's own `accessible_org_ids` (resolved from the delegator's current memberships by `buildContextForUser`, never inherited from the live principal, and fresh on every call) and `this.tenancyPosture` — and refuse on the same reading (`undefined`). Read in `@objectstack/core`, the function answers `undefined` only when a wall is enforced (`postureEnforcesWall`: every posture but `single`) and the set does not hold the claim. So the provider answers the deny sentinel precisely where the find path refuses — a walled posture, a live active organization, a delegator whose membership does not back it — and, as the pins show, on a public, a private and an organization-less object alike, because the rule reads the context and not the object. The ask sits at the prologue's position: after the dangling-delegator mirror, before the delegator's sets resolve.

**(c) Every other cell is unchanged, by construction: right.** `single` (or no posture): the function returns the claim, so the branch does not fire. No active organization: the guard `liveOrganization !== undefined` skips the ask entirely — load-bearing, since the function answers `undefined` for an absent claim — and it is identical to the prologue's guard (ADR-0123 D2 keeps that context). In-set delegated context: the claim is in the delegator's set, the branch does not fire. Undelegated caller: `getReadFilter` never enters the delegated method. Dangling delegator: the sentinel is answered one statement earlier, as before. System context: `getReadFilter`'s `isSystem` exit precedes the delegated branch and is untouched. A principal that resolves no set: the sentinel is answered before the delegator is resolved, as before. The engine's own composition asks the provider only inside the executor behind the middleware chain (find, findOne, count, aggregate), so for an operation the prologue admitted the ask repeats with the same fresh inputs and the same answer; it cannot move an admitted operation.

**(d) The pins are the right cells and are not vacuous: right.** Six refusal cells (two walled postures × three objects) assert the sentinel by identity. Nine preservation cells (per walled posture: in-set delegated, undelegated, no active organization, system; plus `single`) assert "not the sentinel" and then pin the scope by the rows it admits, read as a bypassing door would read it. Two parity cells walk the contexts the prologue decides × the three objects and assert per cell that find refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` ⇔ the provider's sentinel, and where find admits, that the scope admits exactly find's rows — and they assert the refused set itself, so neither side is empty. The ablation and the before/after recording are the dev's runs, not re-run here; the method is sound (the ask is the branch's only conjunct besides the guard, so replacing it with `false` is the rule removed, and the predicted reds are the refusal and parity cells only). No existing pin needed flipping, which the check-runs (③) confirm.

**(e) One bound on the prose, not the code.** "No served door builds the shape" holds at the shipped default; as the precedent record on PR #25101 noted, with the grants cache on (a non-default configuration) the `/mcp` door may hand over a context the prologue then refuses fresh. This diff gives the provider the same fresh answer for that context, which is the fail-closed direction and keeps the lock-step; no overstatement beyond that window.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25106-read-scope-delegated-organization-membership.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-security': patch`, a `fix(plugin-security)!:` title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and the BREAKING banner with FROM, TO, Unchanged and the in-process producer's fix. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines, the arm identical. Level: right. The diff moves one published package and changes nothing an author writes against (no spec key, accepted value, metadata type, meaning or default), so `Metadata-protocol: none` is honest, and under ruling A (#25105) `none` grades `patch` — a `minor` beside `none` is what the level gate now refuses. The arm is right: a context that was answered a composed scope is now answered the deny sentinel and nothing widens, so this is a runtime narrowing, BREAKING under 「甲」 rule 2 as amended (`6303865025`); ruling A keeps the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition on a non-protocol narrowing while re-levelling it to `patch`. That is the precedent's shape (#25063 / PR #25101, which shipped `minor` before ruling A) with the level moved by the later ruling, as the dev's deviation note says. The ADR-0087 arm is consistent with the diff: no declaration is removed or narrowed (one branch in a private method), the package publishes, no ADR-0087 id is named. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The changeset's sentences are the lane seat's at `TIER_DEFAULT`; only the level and the two lines are judged here.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`canReadObject` does not vet the organization** (Acceptance note 1): #25107 is open and carries it. Judged: the row scope's deny is the fail-closed half; object admission is the other half (ADR-0139 D2's split), and the analytics door asks it through `canReadObject` before `getReadFilter`, so after this change the refused shape is admitted at the object level on that door and served zero rows rather than a `403`. Answered: carried by #25107; no change to this verdict.
2. **The stale `plugin-audit` header** (Acceptance note 2; `parent-record-read-gate.ts`, its item 1): verified at this head — it still says the security service's read scope does not carry the delegator intersection, which `getReadFilter`'s own docblock and the engine's composition contradict. The routing it describes (a delegated caller goes to the bounded probe; no leaf is written) stays safe. Documentation drift outside this claim's surface, with no carrier: escalated to the seat to carry (a one-line doc fix, or a row on the #25107 family). No verdict impact.
3. **The parity table's coverage** (Acceptance note 3): right as stated — the table covers the contexts the prologue decides; a grant-intersection refusal is object admission's half for any caller, and the no-active-organization context is pinned in the preservation block, where this diff leaves it byte-identical by the guard in ①(c). Answered.
4. **The system-context observation** (Acceptance note 4): the provider's `isSystem` exit is untouched by this diff and matches its documented mirror of the middleware's system skip; what the engine's find applies for a system context that carries an active organization is not the security middleware's doing and not this rule's. Pre-existing and outside this narrowing: escalated to the seat as an observation to triage (file or dismiss). No verdict impact.
5. **The review owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`** (Acceptance note 5): this record.
6. **`open_questions`**: the final dev report (`6330174654`) carries none. The readings report (`6328225139`) carried one (build the mirror, or close as no-door reach); the seat call `6328262579` answered it (A), and the PR implements A as called — the provider mirror only; no prologue edit, no `canReadObject`, no `service-analytics`, no `plugin-audit`. Answered.
7. **Deviations in the dev report**: the `(narrowing)` arm and the banner added over the claim's bare `Clause-②: no` is the precedent's move and is judged right in ②; the two derived gates NOT MEASURED locally and `test:repo` not run locally are covered by the head's `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core`; the pins living in the rule's existing file is inside the claim's surface. Answered.
8. **Disclosure**: the card, the PR body, the changeset, the two dev reports and this record carry the rule and an abstract reach only; the pins land with the fix and pin the refusal, not the unfixed state.
9. **Check-runs on the head**, read before rendering: 41 runs — 34 success, 7 skipped (conditional or opt-in: Temporal Conformance, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness), 0 failure, 0 pending. Green includes the required Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core and its six shards, Build Core and Governed Surface Queue Guard, plus Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, the four type-check lanes, the lint lanes and the three claim/card guards. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run here.
